tagline: North on US 71, then east the slow way.
intro: From Mena, US 71 runs north into the Ouachita National Forest and on to Waldron, then through Mansfield and Greenwood toward Fort Smith. At Greenwood, Highway 10 takes up the circuit and heads east past Fort Chaffee, through Booneville and Magazine, then over mountainous country past Havana and Danville to Ola.

ARDOT points out that the Ouachitas are the only mountains in North America that run east and west, and gentler country than the Ozarks, which suited the early settlers. Highway 10 was one of the state's original 1926 highways, and even then US 64 was built to a better standard. It is still the slower, scenic way out of Fort Smith.

moments.title: Mena
moments.text: A railroad town from 1896, named by its founder Arthur Stilwell for the wife of his friend and financier, who called her Mena.

moments.title: Jenny Lind
moments.text: A coal town named for a Swedish opera singer. Southeast of it, three quarters of a mile of the original 1920s concrete highway still crosses Bear Creek, bypassed since 1959.

moments.title: Fort Chaffee
moments.text: A camp since 1941, where Elvis Presley spent four days in 1958 and got his first military haircut in Building 803.
